name: High Plank
definition: A strict bilateral bodyweight isometric in which the athlete holds a straight prone bridge on both palms and both feet, with the hands directly under the shoulders, both elbows fully extended, and the feet about hip-width apart. Gravity tends to extend the neutral spine; spine.extension is the resisted tendency, not a dynamic spine.flexion action. NASM directly defines the straight-arm fixture. Lehman measured abdominal activity only in the stable forearm prone bridge; the abs-primary and obliques-secondary hierarchy transfers that family's practical training-emphasis judgment to the same resisted spine.extension tendency. It is not a measurement of the straight-arm lever or an exact-fixture EMG ranking. Can et al. measured serratus-anterior, triceps, and infraspinatus activity in the four-point high plank and reported higher triceps activation than in the low plank. Serratus, external rotators, and triceps receive conservative stabilizer credit consistent with that measured participation for the scapula, shoulder, and locked elbow. Lower-trapezius activity was also measured but is deliberately not assigned because serratus already covers the scapular demand. Palm support loads the wrist toward extension, so finger flexors, which cross the palmar wrist, receive stabilizer credit for the wrist and hand. Gluteus maximus, vasti, and soleus hold the hip, knee, and ankle. The wrist, hand, and lower-body roles are anatomy-and-mechanics assignments, not measured findings. Forearm planks, knee-supported planks, hands-elevated or implement-supported planks, suspension planks, push-ups, shoulder taps, reaches, rows, rotations, walks, and limb lifts remain outside this contract. High Plank uses the same optional added-mass logging convention as Stable Forearm Plank: a coefficient of 1 means measured body mass plus entered added mass. It is not a measured lifted-body share, joint force, or muscle resistance.

exerciseRules.description: Added-load records retain their approved equipment and owner-selected body-mass logging convention.

execution.startingPosition: Place both palms on a stable floor directly under your shoulders with your arms fully extended, and set your feet about hip-width apart.
execution.movement: Lift your body onto your hands and toes and align your head, spine, hips, and heels in one neutral straight line.
execution.endpoint: Hold this position for the set time without letting your hips drop or your lower back sag.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep both elbows straight and the trunk braced without turning the hold into a push-up, hip lift, reach, or limb movement.
execution.supportAndPosture: Press both palms and both feet into the floor and keep breathing while your trunk stays braced.
disqualifyingCompensations: Dropping onto the forearms changes the exercise to a forearm plank.
Bending the elbows lowers the hold out of the straight-arm position.
Piking the hips upward turns the plank into a hip lift.
Lifting a hand or foot turns the hold into a moving-limb plank.
